content:
According to Bloomberg, despite Apple accidentally leaking a demo video showcasing the visual intelligence features of AirPods, the product is "still planned for launch in 2027." The following is the chronology of events.

"Product challenges are still being resolved"

Earlier this week, Apple accidentally included a video in the macOS 26.7 candidate release demonstrating how the AirPods visual intelligence feature works.

Just days after the video surfaced, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in his Power On newsletter as follows:

For years, Apple has been developing AirPods with cameras under the codename B798. As I previously reported, the device was originally slated for a 2026 launch, then pushed back to 2027. However, Apple is also developing another version, codenamed B790 (Apple is known for internally developing multiple competing versions of the same product simultaneously).

Given that Apple accidentally included the video in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, along with the company expecting to hold an iPhone launch event in about a month, the B790 device could potentially be announced at that event.

However, Gurman's latest report indicates that Apple is "still planning to release AirPods with cameras in 2027," despite the leak from the company suggesting the product might arrive sooner.

The report states:

Finally, Gurman noted that the recent leak has further fueled the controversy surrounding the device, with some users opposing AirPods with cameras on privacy grounds. However, he mentioned that these cameras will be low-resolution sensors, not designed to take photos or record video, but rather to "scan the surrounding environment and provide contextual information to the Siri digital assistant and other AI tools."

Whether this will be enough to appease critics who have dubbed the product "pervert headphones" may not be known until next year.
